text:
Jake Sanderson is playing 23:06 a night for Ottawa and the points have dried up. He has ten points in 13 games, but none in his last five, and our numbers do not call him due: the chances have thinned out as well.

The team results are fine. The Senators won four of those five games, and they take 54.14% of shot attempts at 5v5 with Sanderson on the ice. The on-ice expected goals, 50.76%, are a touch worse than when he sits, which is the line to watch for a defenseman Evolving-Hockey ranked fifth in the league in wins above replacement last season. Evolving-Hockey also noted he plays with strong teammates, which flatters raw on-ice numbers.

His tools have not gone anywhere: 99th percentile top speed, a 98.97 mph shot (98th percentile), and he draws more penalties than he takes. One goal on 28 shots is below his normal shooting. When it turns, it usually turns quickly for a player who touches the puck this much.
headline: Jake Sanderson, big minutes and a quiet stretch
